blocks.text: Methods, constructors, and domain operations

Methods describe a value's own behavior: `values.push(item)`, `text.substring(start, end)`, and `file.close()`. Constructors belong to the type they create, as in `File.open(path)`, `Image.image_read(path)`, and `f64.from_bits(bits)`. Domain operations use free functions with named inputs, such as `image_write(path, &image)`, `json_serialize(value)`, and `add_build_file(path, workspace)`. Import the module that owns the operation; importing a domain module does not add all of its operations to every string or byte slice.
Native windows and drawing

`#import "Gui"` exports `Window`, `Input_Types`, `Input`, `Scene`, and `UI`. The current backend requires a Windows x86_64 MSVC target on a Windows host. It builds and caches its bundled native sources with the compiler's embedded Clang and uses Win32 and Direct3D 11; it has no raylib dependency. `create_window` creates a window, `update_window_events` pumps input once per frame, and `begin_render_frame` / `present_frame` bracket rendering. Querying input does not pump the event queue.

`Gui/Scene` supplies meshes, cameras, materials, scene submission, rectangles, and text labels. Window and mesh handles use explicit `destroy_window` and `release_mesh` cleanup. The UI layer keeps its state in a caller-owned `Ui_Context`; widgets need stable nonzero IDs, and input routing uses the preceding frame's widget layout. Keep the context across frames and submit each frame's complete event batch.

Glosso is parsed by a hand-written recursive-descent parser with a precedence-climbing expression loop. The grammar below is written to match that parser production by production rather than to be fed to a generator, so where the parser makes a decision by scanning ahead the grammar says so instead of pretending to be context-free.

Two things the notation cannot carry. Operator precedence and associativity are not in the grammar at all: they live in a table the parser fills in before parsing, from `#operator` declarations in the source dependency graph, which is why the expression production is one flat loop. That mechanism is described in the chapter on the operator prescan, and the standard tiers in the chapter on operator precedence. Token formation is likewise a separate pass; the chapter on punctuation and the token table owns it.
Notation

rows: x repeats zero or more times
a token class produced by the lexer

blocks.text: Tokens

The lexer produces the classes below. `#char` is the one directive the lexer itself interprets. It yields a marked integer token whose origin is retained so the checker can infer `u8`, `s8`, or `rune` for ASCII literals and `rune` for non-ASCII literals. A `\\` at the start of a line yields `MLSTR`, which only `#string` and `#asm` consume.

There are exactly nineteen keywords. `typeclass`, `instance`, `distinct`, `enum_flags`, `true`, `false`, `null`, `mut` and `volatile` are ordinary identifiers that the parser recognises by position, which is why each of them is still legal as a variable name.
Program and declarations

The `definition` alternative is deliberately shared by `::`, `:=`, `::=`, and a typed second `:` or `::`. A definition-shaped initializer therefore creates a named type, procedure, namespace, library, or macro rather than an ordinary constant or global. An explicit annotation describes that declaration value and is checked against its actual kind; without one, the same kind is inferred.

An opening parenthesis does not by itself make a procedure. `K :: (1 + 2) * 3;` and `K :: (42);` are ordinary constants, including inside a body. Parameter syntax and the tokens after the matching `)` distinguish a procedure from a grouped value.

`Namespace` and `Library` are case-sensitive compile-time-only types. `Typeclass(K...)` and `Macro(F)` are parameterized forms recognized in an explicit declaration annotation: `Typeclass` needs at least one parameter kind, and `Macro` takes exactly one procedure signature. They are not generally callable type constructors in ordinary expressions—`row(Typeclass(type))` is an unresolved function call, for example. The old lowercase `namespace`, `library`, and `pattern` type spellings do not resolve.
Aggregates

Every aggregate member ends with `;`, and the diagnostic names the member: a missing one is `error: struct member 'x' must end with ';'`. An enum variant fixes its integer with `::`, not `=`; writing `=` gives `error: enum variant integer values use '::', not '='`. An aggregate written in field position is hoisted to file scope under the name `Owner.field`, which is why `fieldtype` may open a new declaration.

An enum with signed backing may give a variant a negative integer literal, such as `Low :: -1;`. Each named field, variant, and parameter must be unique within its declaration; the blank name `_` may repeat. A struct has at most one `#as` field.
Procedures

The order is fixed and the parser enforces it: parameters, then the return type, then every directive, then every `where` clause, then the body. Reversing the last two is `error: function directives must appear before where clauses`. A body is required unless the declaration is `#magic`, `#foreign`, or a signature-only requirement inside a typeclass. `#operator` is the only operator directive. Its binary and assignment modes take a literal integer level from 0 to 1000, or reuse a level already registered for the spelling. Its unary modes never take a level. A suffix operator may use `#operator(suffix, try(Target))`, where `Target` names its leading `#empty: $Target` witness. It returns `Try_Branch(Try(Source).Output, Target)`: `Continue` supplies the expression's value and `Break` leaves the boundary with the completed carrier. The ordinary operator body performs any residual conversion. All anonymous `#empty:` witnesses must precede runtime parameters. Defaults are evaluated at the call site, so a receiver method cannot refer to `#self` in a parameter default.

A `#expand` procedure with an explicit result other than `void` is a value macro automatically. Its body may contain several statements, branches, and static recursion, provided every reachable path returns a value. The older `#expand,expression` form remains for a macro whose result is inferred; that form must still reduce to exactly one `return <expression>;` (or equivalent static branches).

Control flow in a macro distinguishes its own expansion from its caller explicitly. Plain `return` supplies the macro's value, while prefixing `return` with a backtick leaves the procedure that invoked the macro. Plain `defer` runs inside the macro before its value returns; prefixing `defer` with a backtick registers the statement in the caller. A backtick likewise selects a caller name for reads and writes, not only for declarations.
Typeclasses and instances

An instance is found by scanning forward for a `:::` at bracket depth zero whose next token is the identifier `instance`; everything before that `:::` is the head, taken as raw tokens and re-parsed as a type. `:::` is a dedicated, reserved lexer token; the former `:: instance` spelling is rejected rather than interpreted as an instance. `#minimal` sits between the header and the body, so a `#minimal` written after the closing brace is read as a new declaration and fails with `error: bad decl name 'minimal'`. A member whose body is a type rather than a parameter list is an associated type.
Types

`E!T` binds looser than every prefix modifier and groups to the right, so `Io_Error!?*User` is one result whose payload is `?*User`, and `E1!E2!T` is `E1!(E2!T)`. A parenthesised list is a tuple type unless an `->` follows, in which case it is a procedure type; a single-element list with no name is the parenthesised type itself. An inline `struct`, `union` or `enum` is legal only where a field name is already in hand, and elsewhere gives `error: inline aggregate types are only allowed in aggregate fields`. `[_]T` infers a fixed array's length from its initializer, including a `b"..."` literal; it does not denote a many-pointer.

Two shapes look like grammar but are not. `T.[ ... ]` does not exist: the postfix loop has an arm for `.{` and none for `.[`, so `s64.[1,2]` is the type `s64` followed by a separate array literal, and `for v: s64.[1, 2]` reports `error: 'type' is not iterable; it needs an Iterable instance`. And adjacent operator characters glue into one token, so `E!*T` lexes as the single operator `!*`; the result type of a pointer must be written `E! *T` or `E!(*T)`.
Expressions

The `binop` loop is precedence climbing over a table keyed by operator spelling. An operator with no entry in the table ends the expression, which is how a reserved spelling produces a plain unexpected-token error. Two operators that share a precedence level but disagree about associativity cannot be mixed without parentheses, and the parser says which two.

In value expressions, `&x` and `x.&` take the address of an addressable place; `*p` and `p.*` dereference a typed pointer. The prefix `*` still constructs a pointer when its operand is a type value. `c"..."` has inferred type `cstring` and includes a trailing zero in static storage. `b"..."` has inferred type `[N]u8`, where `N` is its decoded byte count, with no implicit terminator.

Bracket types can also appear as type values: `size_of([]u8)`, `Bytes :: [..]u8;`, and `Container([]u8)` are valid shapes. A generic struct type can qualify its literal, as in `Box(ssize).{ .value = 3 }`. Array and struct literal elements require commas; both forms allow a trailing comma. Chained tuple selection `tuple.0.1` is two member accesses, never a floating-point token.

A `#code` quote may contain a braced statement list, one unbraced statement, or a parenthesised expression such as `#code (a < b)`. The single-statement form borrows its terminator from the surrounding delimiter, which is a contextual exception to the `statement` grammar. `#insert` is a primary expression as well as a statement, declaration, and pattern splice; `#insert,scope() code` resolves a `Code` value in the insertion environment.
error: operators '<+' and '+>' both have precedence 19 but different associativity, so '<+ +>' is ambiguous; add parentheses

An infix `!` is handled by the parser directly rather than through the table, so it works even though `!` carries no precedence, and it stops at `==` followed by `{` so that the switch head is not swallowed. A `..` whose right side is missing becomes a suffix operator, which is what makes `a[2..]` and the pattern range `100..` parse.
Statements

A procedure, struct, enum, union, distinct type, typeclass, or function-pointer alias declared inside a body has lexical scope. A name :: expression binding is a local constant. Ordinary local procedures do not capture runtime locals. A nested distinct and a bodyless nested #foreign or #magic procedure accept an optional semicolon; braced definitions do not. The terminator on a local declaration, assignment, expression statement, value-bearing return, or legacy #asm is waived immediately before } inside a #code quote. Expression-position #inline loops may use a comma after an expression in the generated body. #falling must be the last statement of its arm. An ifx conditional must produce a value on every path.

Patterns

A bare identifier in pattern position binds, which is why matching a named constant needs the `==` marker and why a backticked name refers to the quoting environment instead. A range is not pattern grammar at all: an element that contains `..` or `..=` is parsed as an ordinary expression and converted by `ToPattern`, which is how `100..`, `..=9` and a bare `..` work without a production of their own.
Directives

A directive is lexed as one token class and given meaning by the position it appears in, so the same spelling can mean different things in a declaration, a statement and an expression. The table gives the positions each one is accepted in.

blocks.text: Decisions the grammar defers to lookahead
The parser uses lookahead in the cases below to choose between forms that share an opening token sequence.
An instance is recognised by scanning for the dedicated `:::` token at bracket depth zero followed by the identifier `instance`. Until that token is found, the head is held as raw tokens.
`#pattern` is a test when a `=` appears at depth zero before any `;`, `,` or opening `{`; a `:=` there makes it the bind-or-diverge form; otherwise it is a pattern value.
`==` followed by `{` ends an expression, so `if subject == {` opens a switch instead of comparing against a struct literal.

Inside a body, name :: followed by a procedure signature, struct, enum, union, distinct, typeclass, or #fn_ptr introduces a local declaration. A parenthesized value initializer remains a local constant.
`..` becomes a suffix operator when the token after it can only end an expression, and a `#pattern` element treats `|` as an alternative separator rather than the bitwise operator.
A named parameter list is distinguished from an expression by three tokens: `.`, an identifier, then `=`. Writing `f(name = value)` gives `error: unexpected token '='`.

After a parse error the parser discards tokens until it reaches one in column 1 that can start a declaration: an identifier or operator name followed by `:` or `::`, or one of a small set of top-level directives. A construct indented past column 1 is therefore never a resynchronisation point, and one bad declaration can swallow the indented declarations that follow it.
Memory contract attachment

Effect names and operand shapes are constrained by the contract site. Leading contracts attach to one function or named function-pointer declaration. Calls can carry postfix assertions; historical trailing declaration contracts also accept a bare effect or a parenthesized effect list. The Memory Contracts and Storage Lifetimes chapter lists effects and analysis modes.

Glosso has no diagnostic numbers. The message text is the identifier, so the way to find an entry below is to search for the exact string the compiler printed. The entries use representative names and values; the compiler substitutes those from the program it is checking.

error: unknown function print
  --> …\hello.glo:2:5
  |
2 |     print("hello\n");
  |     ^^^^^
help: did you mean 'tprint'?

Internally a message may carry a `lex error line N: ` or `parse error line N: ` prefix; the renderer strips it, so the prefix never appears in output. Checker diagnostics are collected rather than fatal: several are reported in one run, separated by a blank line, and the run ends with a count. Lexical errors are not collected, because a lexical failure aborts the whole file at once.

  |                   ^^^

  --> …\two.glo:2:18

Driver messages are the only ones with no source frame. They are written to standard error, prefixed `glosso: `, and are produced before any file is read.

A byte view does not convert implicitly to a string view; an explicit `cast(string)bytes` borrows its storage.
Strings are views with read-only descriptors. Assigning to their `.count`, `.data`, or indexed code units reports `left side of assignment is not assignable`.

blocks.text: Operators

rows: Operators are homogeneous: there is no implicit promotion of one operand to the other's type.
`no operator '*' for Meters and Meters: a distinct type gets only the classes it derives; add '#derive(...)' or '#derive,all' on the declaration of 'Meters'`
An operator on a `distinct` type that did not derive the class.
`shift count 8 is not less than the 8 bits of u8`
A compile-time shift count at or past the width, with `note: a shift by the width or more has no defined result`.
`operator '<+>' must be declared by a typeclass and implemented by its instances`
A free operator function at file scope. There are no free operator overloads.
A second class claiming a spelling at the same arity and fixity.
A binary operator declared with no precedence anywhere.
`operator precedence level must be between 0 and 1000`
A level outside the accepted range.
`operators '**' and '~>' both have precedence 19 but different associativity, so '** ~>' is ambiguous; add parentheses`
Mixing two same-tier operators that disagree on associativity.

blocks.text: Typeclasses and instances

rows: Re-declaring a class name. Class names live in one global namespace.

A second typeclass claiming a method name another class already owns. A plain declaration of the same name in a user file gives `function 'show' is owned by typeclass 'Show' and cannot be redeclared` instead.
An instance short of its minimal complete definition, with `note: minimal complete definition declared here`.
`ambiguous typeclass operation 'greet' for these argument types`
Two applicable instances scored equally. Identical semantic instance heads are rejected when declared.
`associated type 'K.Elem' is ambiguous; provide type arguments`
An argument-free projection with more than one supplying instance.
`associated type arguments must follow the typeclass name; write 'K(S).Elem' instead of 'K.Elem(S)'`
Arguments attached to the associated type rather than the class.
`typeclass 'Plain' does not declare a derive macro`
`#derive(C)` for a class with no `#derive` hook of its own.
An evidence query in a position the `where` evaluator cannot fold, such as `where !C(T)` or `where A(T) || B(T)`.

blocks.text: `Try`, `Termination`, and `Show`

rows: `postfix '?' requires a Try-returning function or an enclosing #try block`
`?` with no boundary to break out to.
`?` on a value whose type has no `Try` instance. A type that has one but disagrees about the branch type gives `postfix '?' operand type T does not implement Try`.
`cannot infer the carrier type of #try expression; propagate at least one value with '?'`
A `#try` block with no `?` inside it.
`#try contains one expression; remove the semicolon`
A `#try` block whose single expression ends in `;`. Anything else in the block gives `#try requires one expression`, and a missing block gives `#try requires a block`.
`#try defer requires a Try-returning function or an enclosing #try block`
An error-only defer with no error path to run on.
`main return type Thing does not implement Termination`
A `main` result outside the integers, `E!void`, and types with a hand-written instance.
variadic arg type `Plain` does not implement `Show` in call `print`
A `print` argument with no `Show` instance. The message quotes the type, the class, and the callee in backticks. Expanding a pack gives `expanded variadic element type …` instead.

blocks.text: Control flow, switches, and patterns

rows: `break` at function level, and also inside `#inline while` or a genuinely unrolled `#inline for`, which have no loop to leave.
`'for *x:' needs a PointerIterable instance for string`

A `for *x:` over a type that has an `Iterable` instance but no `PointerIterable` one. A string loop decodes and yields `rune` values, while direct indexing still reads a `u8` or `u16` code unit; decoded values cannot be borrowed.
`'P' is not iterable; it needs an Iterable instance`
A `for` over a type with no `Iterable` instance and no `for_expansion` macro.

A switch the coverage analysis cannot prove total, a tagged-union switch that leaves a variant uncovered included: `if s == { … }` is always a pattern switch. Up to six `note: missing case: …` witnesses follow, then `...and N more`, and last `note: cover them, or add 'else' or '#partial'`.
`cannot switch on a raw union (it has no tag)`
`tagged-union payload '.Circle' may only be bound by a pattern match`
`'Triangle' is not a variant of union U`
A `case` label naming a variant the subject's union does not declare.
`cannot decide a value: an 'ifx' needs an 'else' arm`
The conditional `ifx` without `else`. The switch forms give `cannot decide a value for this ifx` plus the missing cases.
`an ifx arm must end in an expression`
An `ifx` arm whose last statement produces nothing.
`!(#pattern P = e)`, with a `note` pointing at the `#pattern P := e else { … }` form.
`the 'else' of a '#pattern ... :=' binding must not return normally`
A bind-or-diverge `else` that can fall through.
`#if condition must be bool, got comptime_int`
`#if` on a value that is truthy but not `bool`; `#if` is stricter than `if`.
`no label 'nowhere' in this procedure (define it with `'nowhere:`)`
`goto` at a label the procedure does not declare.

blocks.text: Compile-time evaluation

rows: A runtime binding read in a position that must fold, such as a `#if` condition or a range bound in a pattern.
A `#assert` whose condition folds to false. Without a message the text is `assertion failed`.
`#compile_error`; the message is the expression's value, printed with no prefix of its own.
`#inline while condition must be compile-time evaluable`
A runtime condition on an unrolled loop.
`#inline while made no compile-time progress; update a compile-time variable used by the condition`
A body that never changes what the condition reads.
`#inline for` over something other than a tuple or fixed array; a dynamic array gives its own message about runtime length.
`#insert generated invalid source: parse error line 1: unexpected token ';'`
Generated text that does not parse, with a `note` and a frame pointing into the cached generated file.
`#insert needs a Code value or a compile-time string`
A statement or declaration splice whose operand folds to any other value kind.
A modifier other than `scope` after `#insert,`; the accepted form is `#insert,scope(...) value`.
`a 'Code' value is compile-time only; bind it with '::' rather than ':='`
`:=` on a `Code` value. `Pattern` and values produced by named definitions are compile-time-only too.

The legacy inferred-result `#expand,expression` form has a body other than one return statement (or equivalent static branches). Explicitly typed value macros may use a multi-statement body when every path returns; a missing path reports `expanded value macro does not return a value on every path`.
`compile-time execution does not support u129, an integer wider than 128 bits`
A `#comptime { ... }` VM step that executes a value of an integer type wider than 128 bits. Arbitrary-precision constant folding and compiled code are not limited this way.

blocks.text: Memory contracts

Temporal memory findings use warning: by default and error: with --borrow-check=error. They name the memory rule and carry notes for the storage origin, release, or conflicting borrow. --borrow-check=off disables body analysis. Written contracts and memory_strict boundaries are checked separately from managed-value move errors.

rows: `[memory.dangling_return] pointer to local storage escapes through return`
Returning a pointer into a local whose storage ends at function exit.
Releasing an already discharged acquisition obligation.
Access through a tracked resource or derived view after release.
Using a retained view after its storage was invalidated.
`[memory.X1] noalias argument overlaps another live reference`
A call violates the unique-access promise of a noalias parameter.
`body of 'modify' has undeclared writes effect on 'value'`
The implementation writes through a parameter that its contract did not permit it to write.
`exported function 'view' requires a #memory contract under memory_strict`
An exported memory boundary lacks a written contract in a strict module.
An acquired raw resource reaches scope exit without release, ownership transfer, or an explicit permitted opt-out.

blocks.text: Warnings

Warnings use the identical layout with `warning:` in place of `error:`. Besides the temporal-analysis family above there are three, and all three point at code that compiles but probably does not mean what it says.

rows: `this expression changes meaning under the 0-20 precedence table: bitwise operators now bind tighter than comparisons`
An unparenthesised bitwise expression as an operand of a comparison, or the reverse, as in `flags & mask == 4`. It carries `note: add parentheses to say which reading you mean`.
`unreachable pattern - already covered by an earlier case`
An arm of a `#pattern` switch that the arms above it already cover.
`no '+' for <T>: the where-clause only provides Addable`

A generic definition uses an operator whose owning typeclass is absent from the parameter's `where` evidence. It is reported at the definition and carries `note: reported at the definition; add the class to the 'where' clause`.

blocks.text: Runtime messages

A program can also print. Runtime messages come from the compiled program, not the compiler, are written to standard error, and are followed by the target's abort path. Array bounds, union-tag failures, and assertions name a source position when available; the shorter category reports do not.

…\k11.glo:5:46: union access: expected .Box, but the value holds one of .Circle | .Box
glosso: program exited with status exit code: 134

rows: `union access: expected .Box, but the value holds one of .Circle | .Box`
An `#enable(allow_union_unwrap)` payload read whose tag check failed at `-O0` or `-O1`.
A `#assert` whose condition was not compile-time known and was false at run time.
`cast to *s64 of an address that is zero`
A runtime `cast(*s64)` of a null address; another destination type is named when one was written.
The debug allocator, enabled by a nonzero `GLOSSO_DEBUG_ALLOCATOR`, at exit; each leak is listed with its allocation site.
The same allocator on a repeated release. Use-after-free, invalid free, and invalid realloc have matching lines.
Checked integer addition, subtraction, multiplication, or negation overflowed.
A checked integer division or remainder used zero, or signed division evaluated `MIN / -1`.
A checked index was outside an array, view, `string`, or `string16` count. C-string indexing does not scan for a bound.
A checked slice range was negative, inverted, or extended past the source count.
`value.format_int` used an unsupported base in a checked build.

blocks.text: These backend guards are emitted only at `-O0` and `-O1`. Hosted Windows and Linux x86-64 terminate them with status 134, WASI uses 125, and the remaining targets call `abort()`. At `-O2` and `-O3`, overflow and bounds guards are absent; bad division reaches LLVM and the target hardware instead of a Glosso report.

The compiler enforces none of what follows. These are the conventions the standard library holds to, and the reason to hold to them is that a program spends most of its text calling that library: code written in the same shapes reads as one body of work rather than two.
Naming

There are four name shapes and the shape says what kind of thing the name binds. Nothing in the language reads a name's case, so the shape is carrying information the compiler does not: a reader who sees `Slot_Table` knows it is a type before finding the declaration.

rows: a `__` prefix on the usual shape

blocks.text: The library holds this line exactly: of more than three thousand top-level procedures in `std`, not one is spelled in camel case. The typeclass exception is deliberate. A class name appears inside type expressions, in `where` clauses, and as an instance head, always beside real type names, and dropping the underscores is what keeps `where Eq(T) && Hash(T, DefaultHasher)` legible.
A procedure that operates on a type is named after that type: the module prefix comes first and the verb second, so every operation on a value sorts together in a listing and in a completion menu.

Names collide across the whole program, so the prefix habit is doing real work. A typeclass method name is reserved with no import at all: `show :: (x: ssize) -> ssize { … }` is `error: function 'show' is owned by typeclass 'Show' and cannot be redeclared`, and so are `next`, `from_string`, and every operator name. Anything an import brings in collides too: with `#import "Math";` in the file, `PI :: 3.14;` is `error: constant 'PI' is already declared` and `abs` is `error: function 'abs' is already declared`.
Layout
Four spaces per level, never a tab. There is not one tab character in `std`.
Lines wrap near 80 columns; nine lines in ten of the library are under 76.
The opening brace stays on the line that opened the construct, and the closing brace sits at the owner's indentation.
One blank line between top-level declarations; none inside a short body.

Semicolons terminate top-level declarations that do not end in their own definition body, and ordinary simple statements inside bodies. A small set of statement forms accepts an optional `;`; switch case and `else` labels require one, and a label statement requires `;` or the legacy `:`. The library writes semicolons consistently.

A signature too long for one line breaks after the open parenthesis, puts one parameter per line, keeps a trailing comma on the last one, and returns the `)` to the declaration's indentation. Directives and `where` clauses then go on their own lines, in that order, before the body's brace.

A switch puts its `case` labels one level inside the braces, not at the brace's own indentation. A one-line arm follows its label on the same line; anything longer starts on the next line, indented once more. The pattern is worth keeping because a `case` label is not a block and a reader needs the indentation to see where an arm ends.
File and declaration order

Nothing in Glosso requires an order: `main` may call a procedure declared below it, and `#import` may sit at the bottom of the file. The library still fixes one, because a file read top to bottom should introduce a name before it is used.

rows: A header comment naming the file and stating in one line what it is for, then a short paragraph of what a caller must know.
The module's error type, then its data types, then its typeclasses and instances.
Constructors, then queries, then mutators, then the destructor, grouped by the type they belong to.
Private helpers, optionally prefixed with `#private`; ordinary declarations are file-private by default.

blocks.text: Visibility prefixes apply to a declaration or a transparent braced group. `#public { ... }` exports that group's declarations; a nested `#private` overrides it and the enclosing default resumes afterward. Use `#public(unit)` when helpers should be shared across source files in one ownership unit. The removed `private_section` and `siblings` feature-gate spellings produce migration diagnostics.

The entry file's `main` may keep its default private visibility. Language visibility and native symbol export are separate: `#c_call` still supplies library entry points, while another Glosso module needs an accessible declaration to use their Glosso names.
Documenting ownership

Document whether an API moves an owner, borrows storage, returns a fresh allocation, or transfers a raw buffer to the caller. Describe mutation that invalidates views and the allocator or foreign function needed to release raw results. Use Drop for automatic cleanup and pointers for helpers that leave ownership with their caller.
When to reach for a typeclass

A typeclass is the only overloading mechanism the language has, so the question is never "class or free function" but "class or generic procedure". A `where` clause on a generic procedure says what the caller's type must already be able to do; a typeclass says what a type must newly declare. Prefer the former until a second implementation exists.
One behaviour, many types, each needing its own body: a typeclass. `Show` and `Hash` are this.
One body that works for every type meeting a condition: a generic procedure with `where`. No class is needed.
A new operator spelling: a typeclass, always. An operator must have exactly one owning class, and a free operator function is rejected.
A name that must be callable before its implementations exist, such as a callback a library invokes: a typeclass, so the library can constrain on it.
A marker with no methods: a typeclass with `#minimal()`, queried with `#if C(T)`.

Give every class parameter a position in every method's signature. A default method that omits one cannot be dispatched, because nothing at the call site decides it; an anonymous `#empty:` witness parameter is the standard way to give a type a position without giving it a value. State the minimal definition with `#minimal` even when it is a single name, because that is what turns an incomplete instance into one error at the instance rather than a missing overload at every call.

Instance selection is ordinary overload resolution, so it runs through implicit coercions: a concrete `s64` instance will capture a `u32` argument, because `u32` widens losslessly and a concrete parameter scores higher than a generic one. When an instance must key on exactly one type, write a blanket instance guarded by `where T == s64` rather than a concrete head.
Errors

A procedure that can fail returns `E!T`; a procedure whose only failure is absence returns `?T`. The library gives each module one error type named after the module, propagates with `?` rather than hand-written branching, and widens between modules with `#from` variants so a caller's union absorbs a callee's error without a conversion function.

n = 17
bad number: nope

That program exits with status 1 and prints its report to standard error, without a line of exit-code handling: `main` returning `App_Error!void` dispatches through `Termination`, which reports the error and returns 1. Reserve `#assert` for conditions a caller cannot cause and an error value for everything a caller can.
Comments

The library comments the contract, not the mechanism. A file header is a `//!` block stating what the module is for and what a caller must guarantee; a declaration carries a `///` block stating the invariant a reader could not derive from the signature, under `#` headings of which `# Errors`, `# Ownership` and `# Invalidation` are the common three. Line comments inside a body are rare, and `// ----` section rules divide long files.
Say what a caller must guarantee, not what the next statement does.
Put the ownership story in the header: who allocates, who releases, what invalidates what.
Name a known limitation where a reader will hit it, rather than in a change log.
A `/* */` comment nests, so it is safe to comment out a region that already contains one; an unterminated one is the lexical error `unterminated block comment`.
